directAnswer: Pope Nicholas IV was Girolamo Masci of Ascoli, the first Franciscan to become pope, who reigned from 22 February 1288 to 4 April 1292. A former minister general of his order, he sent John of Montecorvino on the mission that brought Catholic preaching to China, approved a rule for the Franciscan Third Order, and saw the fall of Acre, the last crusader stronghold in the Holy Land.

sections.h2: Successor of Bonaventure as Minister General
paras: Girolamo Masci was born near Ascoli in the Marche and joined the Franciscans young. He served as a papal envoy to Constantinople under Gregory X in connection with the planned church union, and in 1274 he succeeded St. Bonaventure as minister general of the Franciscan Order. Nicholas III created him a cardinal, and he later became cardinal bishop of Palestrina.

When Honorius IV died in 1287, the conclave dragged on for nearly eleven months, slowed by an epidemic that killed several cardinals. Girolamo, who had stayed in Rome through the summer, was finally elected in February 1288 and took the name Nicholas in memory of Nicholas III, who had made him a cardinal.

sections.h2: Missions to the Mongols and to China
paras: Nicholas took a strong interest in the peoples of Asia. He exchanged letters with the Mongol ruler of Persia and received the envoy Rabban Sauma, a Christian monk from China who traveled to Europe and received Communion from the pope in Rome in 1288.

In 1289 he sent the Franciscan John of Montecorvino east with letters for the Mongol rulers, including the Great Khan. John reached Khanbaliq, modern Beijing, in the 1290s and founded the first Catholic mission there, later becoming its archbishop. The mission is one of the lasting results of Nicholas's pontificate.

sections.h2: The Third Order, Montpellier and Santa Maria Maggiore
paras: In 1289 Nicholas issued the bull Supra montem, which gave a formal rule to the Brothers and Sisters of Penance, the lay movement that became the Franciscan Third Order. The same year he granted university status to the schools of Montpellier, and he issued the constitution Caelestis altitudo, which assigned half of the revenues of the Roman Church to the College of Cardinals.

He also left his mark on Rome's churches. He rebuilt the apse of the Lateran basilica and especially of Santa Maria Maggiore, where the Franciscan artist Jacopo Torriti created the mosaic of the Coronation of the Virgin that still dominates the apse. Nicholas chose Santa Maria Maggiore as his burial place.

In May 1291 the Mamluk sultan captured Acre, ending two centuries of crusader presence on the mainland of the Holy Land. Nicholas responded by calling for a new crusade, asking provincial councils to consider uniting the military orders, and seeking help from European rulers, but no expedition followed. His reliance on the Colonna family in Roman affairs also drew criticism.
He died in Rome on 4 April 1292. The cardinals then remained divided for more than two years, a vacancy ended only by the unexpected election of the hermit Pietro da Morrone.

keyFacts: Born Girolamo Masci near Ascoli; first Franciscan pope
Minister general of the Franciscans after St. Bonaventure (1274)
Sent John of Montecorvino to the Mongol court in China (1289)
Gave a rule to the Franciscan Third Order with Supra montem (1289)
Pope when Acre fell to the Mamluks in 1291
Died in Rome, 4 April 1292; buried in Santa Maria Maggiore

faqs.question: Was Nicholas IV the first Franciscan pope?
faqs.answer: Yes. Girolamo Masci, a former minister general of the Order of Friars Minor, was the first Franciscan elected pope, in 1288.

faqs.question: How was Nicholas IV connected to Catholic missions in China?
faqs.answer: In 1289 he sent the Franciscan John of Montecorvino to the Mongol rulers. John established the first Catholic mission in Beijing and later became its first archbishop.

faqs.question: What can visitors see of Nicholas IV in Rome today?
faqs.answer: The apse mosaic of the Coronation of the Virgin at Santa Maria Maggiore, made by Jacopo Torriti, was commissioned during his reign, and his tomb is in the same basilica.
